# IEBP001: get_model_location

<!-- Generated by `python -m inspect_evals_lint.docs`; edit the source, not this file. -->

Resolve models and inspect model roles during solver, scorer or agent execution.

**Category:** best_practices · **Applies to:** eval, helper

## What it does

Warns when `get_model()` or `model_roles()` can run during module, task, solver, scorer or agent construction. A decorator such as `@scorer` registers a factory; its body runs before the inner scoring function does. Defaults and decorators on the returned callback run when the factory defines it.

The rule follows named functions returned by component factories and direct calls to package helpers, including imports and re-exports within the package. Helpers reached only during execution pass. A helper reached during construction as well is reported at its lookup.

## Why is this bad?

A task can be constructed before `eval()` receives its model roles. Resolving a role in a factory can select the fallback before the runner's chosen model is available. A `model_roles()` check at that point also misses the runner's binding, including a list of graders.

## Example

```python
@scorer(metrics=[accuracy()])
def graded():
    grader = get_model(role="grader", default=DEFAULT_GRADER)

    async def score(state, target):
        return await grader.generate(state.input_text)

    return score
```

Use instead:

```python
@scorer(metrics=[accuracy()])
def graded():
    async def score(state, target):
        grader = get_model(role="grader", default=DEFAULT_GRADER)
        return await grader.generate(state.input_text)

    return score
```

This example selects one model for a custom scorer. For a built-in `model_graded_*` scorer, inspect `model_roles()` inside `score()` and leave a configured role to the built-in scorer. See the [grader-role guidance](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/blob/main/BEST_PRACTICES.md#use-model-roles-for-multi-model-evals). Constructing a built-in scorer with `model_role=...` is allowed; that scorer resolves the role when it runs.

## Known limits

The analysis follows named package functions, not arbitrary callbacks, method dispatch, function aliases assigned to variables, or calls through other packages. A lookup with no known runtime path is reported as well; helpers whose runtime callers are outside the checked package may need a suppression explaining how they are invoked. Calls imported under aliases are not recognised. Conditional branches are all considered possible.
